memory_update.text: MIDD should remain the primary underfollowed/mid-cap candidate for the commercial kitchen equipment and service node because its filings directly mention commercial foodservice equipment, restaurant operators, service agents, parts warehouses and quick-ship support.
ITW is a reference leader, not an underfollowed alpha candidate, but it provides an important benchmark for food-equipment brands, factory-trained service networks and segment economics.

DOV maps to the refrigeration/cold-chain portion of the node through Dover Food Retail, Hillphoenix, Anthony and CO2 refrigeration systems; restaurant purity must be verified because supermarket/food-retail exposure may dominate.

The strongest installed-base service companies in commercial kitchen repair, certified technicians, warranty administration and parts distribution may be private; Layer 1C should search for public distributors, roll-ups, warranty administrators, HVAC/refrigeration service firms and restaurant facility-service providers.

FARM is a speculative-shadow micro-cap with unusually direct beverage equipment service and DSD exposure; it should not survive later layers without proof of recurring service economics, customer retention and balance-sheet viability.

node: Commercial kitchen, beverage, refrigeration, and equipment service networks
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a compact US-listed universe around the restaurant equipment/service node. The cleanest direct exposure is Middleby, a mid-cap commercial foodservice equipment leader with parts/logistics/service-agent infrastructure. ITW is the obvious reference leader through its Food Equipment segment and factory-trained service network, but restaurant exposure is diluted inside a large industrial. Dover is a near-large-cap/large-cap industrial with meaningful refrigeration and food-retail infrastructure exposure, relevant to cold-chain uptime and lower-GWP refrigeration upgrades, though not restaurant-pure. Farmer Bros. is a micro-cap speculative exception: its coffee/beverage DSD network and equipment-servicer role make it a possible hidden service-network beneficiary, but financial fragility and small market cap require strict verification.
